environment.description: Same Laravel 10.x application deployed behind Cloudflare with a Page Rule applying a Transform Rule on the zone. The Cloudflare managed transform rule 'Managed Transforms > Add security headers' is enabled which appends a Content-Security-Policy response header. However, the specific CSP directive applied is configured via a Cloudflare Worker that runs on the route pattern /messages/* which sets the header to: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'. The worker executes after the origin response and before delivery to client. Note: the CSP does NOT include 'unsafe-inline' for script-src, and does not include 'unsafe-eval'. The nonce-based CSP is not used here - it relies on allowlisting. The Cloudflare Worker also strips any existing CSP headers from the origin to prevent header duplication. Additionally, the zone has Cloudflare's 'Browser Integrity Check' enabled which performs basic bot detection but is not relevant to this specific attack vector.

config.worker_csp_header: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
